newsitem.title: USA: Country singer Faron Young dies in suicide.
newsitem.headline: Country singer Faron Young dies in suicide.

text.p: Country music singer Faron Young died on Tuesday, a day after he shot himself in the head, his family said.
Young became famous with a major hit in in the early 1960s, "Hello Walls," written by Willie Nelson and came back with a surprise hit in 1972 with "Four in the Morning."

He worked on the Louisiana Hayride radio show early in his career before signing with Capitol Records in 1952. He founded Music City News but eventually sold the publication, now the largest circulation music magazine in the United States.

Young, 64, had a history of alcohol-related problems. In recent months he had suffered from emphysema and had undergone prostate surgery. Nashville police said on Monday he had left a suicide note saying he was depressed over health problems.

Young's family issued a statement saying the performer died in the early afternoon and "left his family, friends and fans to perform the biggest concert of his career." He had been at Columbia Summit Medical Centre in Nashville for about 24 hours after a former band member found him seriously injured at his home.
